gate.name: complexity_tier
gate.description: Classify a request into exactly one complexity tier using a two-dimensional matrix: reasoning depth (logical hops, hypothesis-verification cycles) and execution scope (files, integrations, structural breadth). Rules: (1) Depth overrides scope — a task needing BOTH massive scope AND high multi-hop reasoning is reasoning. (2) Not all bugs are reasoning — an error pointing to the exact fault (e.g. 'SyntaxError: expected } at line 42') is medium; a vague failure or an error that does not reflect the root cause (e.g. 'app randomly crashes in production') is reasoning. (3) Judge by signal-to-noise ratio, not word count — a short prompt needing deep deduction, or a huge noisy log hiding a single clue, are both reasoning.

classes.label: simple
classes.description: Low reasoning depth and low execution scope. Covers BOTH: (a) trivial single-step technical fixes — typos, a CSS/hex value change, an API glossary lookup, a document update; and (b) no actionable task — administrative notes, project-tracker checklists, or feature-request/bug-report descriptions that ask for no code, design, or analysis. No synthesis or structural understanding required.
utterances: Feature request describing a small UI preference change, with no implementation details requested
Project tracker checklist marking rollout steps as completed or still pending
Question asking when a feature will ship in the next release
Bug report noting a missing setting label, with a one-line fix
The README quick start still shows the old install command and needs updating
There is a typo in an error message string that should be corrected
Rename a variable in one file to match the naming convention
The brand color in the stylesheet is a hardcoded hex value and needs replacing
The documentation lists a default value that no longer matches the code
Reserve an issue number for an upcoming fix, with no technical detail yet

classes.label: medium
classes.description: Moderate reasoning depth, low-to-moderate scope. Standard engineering or API-design work with a linear solution path: the target file, required action, or root cause is stated explicitly in the prompt or error log. Example: 'SyntaxError: expected } at line 42' — the fault is evident, so fix it directly. Apply existing knowledge; do not investigate root causes.
utterances: Add pagination to the existing list endpoint following the pattern already used by the session list
The stack trace points to a null dereference at a specific line, fix that site
Wire a new configuration flag from the settings schema through to the handler
Extract this repeated logic into a shared helper function
Add a unit test covering the edge case described in the report
Update the client to use the new error type across all call sites
The error message says the module is missing, so install and import it
Implement a small feature with a clearly specified interface and requirements
Add validation for a new input field with an explicit schema
Migrate a single component to the new hooks pattern

classes.label: complex
classes.description: Low-to-moderate reasoning depth, HIGH execution scope. The solution path is KNOWN and deterministic, but execution spans many files, services, or dependencies: schema migrations, bulk mechanical refactors, vendor upgrades, full CRUD boilerplate across 10+ files. High effort, no detective work. Contrast: 'migrate the schema across 10 services' = complex; 'find the race hidden across 10 files' = reasoning.
utterances: Migrate the database schema across every service that depends on it
Upgrade the vendored dependency and update every call site in the repository
Generate the full CRUD scaffolding for this entity from the specification
Apply the same mechanical refactor across more than ten files
Coordinate version bumps across multiple repositories in one release
Roll out the new API contract to every client integration
Deprecate the legacy interface across all remaining components
Split the monolith into two services and wire up a message queue between them
Introduce multi-tenancy with per-tenant schema isolation across the stack
Implement an event-driven pipeline with an outbox and dead-letter handling

classes.label: reasoning
classes.description: High reasoning depth at ANY scope. The solution path is UNKNOWN or non-linear: form and test hypotheses, trace subtle interactions, evaluate trade-offs, or filter noise to find a hidden root cause. Examples: race conditions, memory leaks, flaky or intermittent failures, 'app randomly crashes in production', a root cause hidden in a massive unstructured log dump, a novel algorithm, or contradictory architectural constraints. Depth overrides scope.
utterances: Diagnose the intermittent crash that only reproduces in production
Root-cause the race condition between the two background workers
Trace the memory leak that appears only after several hours of load
Investigate why this flaky test fails only under load
The app randomly crashes in production with no obvious trigger, find the root cause
Find the single clue hidden in this large unstructured log dump
Prove that this locking scheme cannot deadlock
Reason about the security implications of this trust boundary
Determine why the garbage collector pauses spike under allocation pressure
Reconstruct the sequence of events that corrupts the checkpoint file
